hero.title: P&G – Conditioning product packaging
hero.oneLiner: A sponsored studio on how a conditioning bottle is held, dispensed, and kept in a haircare routine.

context.text: Five of us at Northwestern EDI worked with P&G on conditioning product packaging. We ran 8 in-home visits and 2 central-site rounds, synthesized what we saw, and tested 10 bottle form studies. The public page is the process. Pack artwork and mechanisms stay under NDA.

bullets: Ran in-home visits focused on hold, storage, and the routine around the bottle
Wrote the CSV2 research synthesis the team used to set requirements
Modeled and printed bottle form studies for hands-on comparison
Tested those forms across two central-site rounds

decisions.decision: Study the routine, not a finished pack
decisions.why: The useful questions were how the bottle is held, where it lives, and how it is dispensed.
decisions.tradeoff: The public case cannot show the final artwork or the mechanism.

decisions.decision: Ten form studies instead of one polished concept
decisions.why: A difference in proportion or grip had to be something a person could hold.
decisions.tradeoff: Early forms are diagrams of the question, not the sponsor's pack.

worked: In-home visits made the bathroom routine visible in a way a survey would not.
Printed forms gave the central-site rounds something specific to handle.
didnt: Final packs and the detailed findings stay confidential, so this page stops at the process.

outcome.text: The team presented a packaging direction. This page keeps the research, the form studies, and the testing rounds, and leaves the sponsor's packs off the public site.

reflection.text: The bottle was never just an object in the hand. It sat inside a routine, and the routine is what the visits were for.
